Los mapas precargados no son del proyect: The bundled maps are not part of this project: they come from the game's textures. The dropdown below switches between the ones in the catalogue (data/maps.json). To use others, drop them on the drop area or leave them in data/.

El mapa de biomas de SCANsat (720×360) v: The SCANsat biome map (720×360) works as it is: it is 2:1 and is drawn without interpolation. The degrees box on each row rotates that map in longitude, since not every map out there uses KSP's prime meridian. If you load colour and biome, the button above works the offset out on its own.
Los nombres los pones tú: la paleta camb: You name the biomes yourself: the palette changes between versions and exporters, so the viewer guesses none of them. Click a row to name it. They are kept on your computer and you can export them to reuse later.
El terreno de Kerbin stock es <b>procedu: Stock Kerbin's terrain is procedural: the PQS generates it from noise, so there is no height texture inside the game to extract. This is only useful if you get a greyscale heightmap on your own, and even then the greys carry no scale: it has to be calibrated.
Para calibrar: pulsa «Punto A», haz clic: To calibrate: press «Point A», click somewhere whose real altitude you know (the game tells you when you land there) and type it in. Repeat with B somewhere at a clearly different altitude and the range sorts itself out.
There is no pixel to read there.
El relieve necesita un mapa de alturas c: The relief needs a height map loaded. Exaggerate it so that it shows: at real scale, Kerbin's highest peak is 1% of the radius and nothing would be visible.
Arrastra para girar, rueda para acercart: Drag to turn, wheel to zoom in: you can go all the way down to the ground. As you get closer the camera tilts towards the horizon (the arrow keys change the heading) and, near the ground, the detailed relief, close-up textures, vegetation and buildings are loaded, with more detail the closer you are. Markers hide themselves when they pass behind the horizon.
Ponte de pie en cualquier punto de Kerbi: Stand anywhere on Kerbin and look up: the vessels in your save cross the sky at the pace of the time bar. Drag to look around, the wheel zooms and the arrow keys turn the view too.
El Sol va donde lo pone la órbita de Ker: The Sun sits where Kerbin's orbit puts it at the moment shown on the time bar (with no save loaded, the start of the game): by day the sky is blue, at sunset the horizon lights up and at night the stars come out. «Force night» turns the day off so vessels are easier to follow. The stars are decorative, but they turn with Kerbin as real ones would.

La barra de tiempo de abajo mueve todas: The time bar at the bottom moves every vessel: pause (space), faster forwards (.) or backwards (,), and «Saved» returns to the moment of the save. Click a vessel to see its ground track and press «Follow» (F) so the camera keeps it; dragging cancels that. It is pure Kepler: going backwards you see where each vessel would have been according to its current orbit, with no manoeuvres, and an orbit that grazes the atmosphere does not slow down. The longitude adjustment corrects every vessel at once; normally it is not needed.

Elige una nave en órbita, pon el objetiv: Pick a vessel in orbit, put the target where you want to set down, and the viewer works out when to burn and how much, with a single retrograde burn. It draws the descent on the map and on the globe. With no atmosphere the result is exact but for the terrain; with an atmosphere it is an estimate: the braking depends on the craft, and the ballistic coefficient (mass over Cd times area) is the knob for tuning it.
